Commentary.Commentary: We are ready for New Zealand's reply with the bat! The players have already taken over the field. Georgia Plimmer and Isabella Gaze will be opening for the White Ferns. For South Africa, Marizanne Kapp will start with the new ball as usual. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Mammoth chase ahead - As the Kiwis prepare to embark on this mammoth run chase, they will need a good and strong start from the top order of the batting unit. On the other end, the Proteas' bowling unit have enough runs on the board, so they can totally focus on attacking the batters to pick early wickets. The stage is set for a riveting second innings, so stay tuned as it might start any time soon.

From trouble to triumph - But little did the White Ferns know that their opposition were far from done. Nadine de Klerk and Chloe Tryon dug in and forged a formidable partnership that frustrated the Kiwi bowlers and made the breakthrough feel an eternity away. The pair put on 90 runs together, steadily rebuilding the innings and shifting the momentum back in South Africa's favour. It was ultimately captain Amelia Kerr who provided the breakthrough, but by the time she managed to separate the duo in the penultimate over, the damage had already been done, and the Proteas had enough on the board to set a challenging target.

Crucial breakthroughs - After being asked to bat first, South Africa's top order endured a shaky start, losing two batters for single-digit scores in quick succession. It was captain Laura Wolvaardt who held the innings together, stepping up with composure and authority to shoulder the responsibility at a critical juncture. However, Jess Kerr proved to be the standout performer with the ball, dismissing the dangerous Wolvaardt to give New Zealand a much-needed breakthrough, while Sophie Devine removed the experienced Marizanne Kapp to leave the Proteas in a precarious position.

Proteas surge - Phew... that was some inning for the Proteas. In the first ten overs, the game was equally poised, but as soon as Chloe Tryon and Nadine De Klerk kept on hitting, the scoreline had a spike. At one point, it even looked like they were taking revenge for what happened in Dubai on 20th October 2024.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of New Zealand Women. It will be the pairing of Laura Wolvaardt and Sune Luus to open the innings for South Africa Women. It will be the off-spin of Nensi Patel to get things underway with the ball. Let's go...

The skipper of South Africa Women - Laura Wolvaardt says that she's fine with batting first, but wanted to bowl first to shake things up a bit. She informs that they are playing with the same combination and on their first game against Australia, she says that their focus for now is on this game. Ends by saying that there are a few butterflies heading into the main event, but they will look to put their best foot forward.

The captain of New Zealand Women - Amelia Kerr, with a big smile, says they will be bowling first. She continues that today is a very key game for them and they will try to bring in different conditions to see if it works out or not. About their opposition, she says that the Proteas are a very hard opposition and they will take the match seriously.

New Zealand Women - Amelia Kerr (C), Bree Illing, Brooke Halliday, Flora Devonshire, Georgia Plimmer, Isabella Gaze, Izzy Sharp, Jess Kerr, Lea Tahuhu, Maddy Green, Nensi Patel, Polly Inglis, Rosemary Mair, Sophie Devine, and Suzie Bates.

South Africa Women - Annerie Dercksen, Ayabonga Khaka, Chloe Tryon, Dane Van Niekerk, Karabo Meso, Kayla Reyneke, Laura Wolvaardt, Marizanne Kapp, Nadine De Klerk, Nonkululeko Mlaba, Shabnim Ismail, Sinalo Jafta, Sune Luus, Tazmin Brits, and Tumi Sekhukhune.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Amelia Kerr. New Zealand Women will BOWL first.

White Ferns looking to go back-to-back - The White Ferns enter the tournament with the supreme confidence of reigning champions, backed by a roster that blends seasoned legends with high-impact youth. Their primary focus will be adapting to the bounce and pace of the local pitches while ensuring their primary match-winners stay sharp. So, which side will head into the main event with a big 'W' against their name? We shall find out in due course. Stay tuned for the toss.

Proteas looking to go one step further - South Africa, runners-up in the 2024 edition, boast an incredibly explosive top order but have occasionally struggled with lower-middle-order consistency and defensive bowling execution under pressure. Because warm-up regulations permit teams to utilize their entire squad across batting and bowling departments, expect South Africa to experiment heavily with their combinations.

White Ferns vs Proteas - Hello, and a warm welcome to our coverage of the ICC Women's World Cup, 2026 warm-ups. In Match 10, the reigning champions, New Zealand Women, will be going up against the team they beat to win the trophy in 2024, South Africa Women. We have already seen a game take place at Loughborough today, where Ireland Women beat Bangladesh Women in a spin-to-win battle. Expect another enticing contest as two top teams go up against each other.
... MATCH DAY ...

Time for final preparations - As the countdown to the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 approaches its final leg, a massive heavyweight clash awaits in the warm-ups. A highly anticipated rematch of the previous edition's finalists sees South Africa Women square off against New Zealand Women at Loughborough. With the main tournament kicking off on June 12, this Match 10 fixture represents a vital laboratory for both camps to solidify their final XI, adjust to the local conditions, and seize critical psychological momentum.
